02 / Capital Efficiency & Community Voice

Engagement per Public Dollar.

Customer satisfaction (stars and sentiment) did not systematically track public spending (r ≈ 0.00, failed placebo test). We evaluate where public capital actually moved commercial participation and review volume. Compare net review gains and active business expansion across project investments.

Does the picture depend on the lag?

Every lag from zero to three years is shown. The outlined bar is your selection.

Same ZIP cohort across lags

A taller bar is not evidence of the “right” lag. Trying many lags can produce a striking pattern by chance. This sensitivity view uses only ZIPs with valid outcomes and complete funding-window history at every tested lag; its cohort can differ from the scatterplot.

Study regionCovered populationWindow fundingFunding / residentReview sentimentCovered ZCTAs

These are project-defined mapped study areas, not official city or metro populations. Population coverage uses the current minimum-population setting; zero and missing populations are always excluded. Regional sentiment is review-weighted across those same covered ZCTAs that meet the review threshold in the selected quarter. Funding rates are not amounts received by individual residents.

Population is the Census TIGERweb 2020 ZCTA population count (POP100), held fixed throughout 2012–2021. This supports a comparison of scale; it does not estimate historical per-capita spending. Tiny residential populations can produce extreme rates. An office ZIP can record funding that benefits a much larger region.

04 / Inside the reviews

What are people talking about?

Overall sentiment mixes many experiences. Separate reviews mentioning parking or surroundings from reviews about service, price and products, then carry that lens back to the map.

Selected quarter · overlapping text tags
Text categories have not been built. Run the review-topic pipeline to enable this section.

Mentions, not conclusions

Share of all reviews in this area and quarter. Select a theme to filter sentiment throughout the page.

Rules search for words and phrases, and a review may match several themes. A cleanliness mention can be praise or a complaint; it may refer to a bathroom, not a street. Theme sentiment is the score of the whole review, not the sentiment of that specific aspect.

Look beyond the average

Star ratings for all reviews in the selected area and quarter, regardless of theme.

Stars and text sentiment measure different things. Yelp reviews are self-selected, and business or reviewer composition can change over time.

Read the language behind a tag

Short excerpts from a seeded sample, balanced across whole-review sentiment classes within each city, year and theme. They illustrate matching language and are not a representative estimate. Scores apply to the full review. No reviewer identities are included.

The next analytical step

Validate the tags before interpreting them.

Human-label reviews across cities and years, measure precision and recall for each theme, and distinguish business interiors from the surrounding area. Then compare these transparent rules with a text classifier. These exploratory tags give us a testable starting point.

About the data & how to read this map

This atlas explores associations between federal funding and business-review sentiment, not whether funding caused a change. Yelp measures experiences with businesses, not a representative survey of neighborhood well-being. Reviews cover full quarters from 2012 through 2021 in the January 2022 dataset.

City views are project-defined ZIP groups. Map polygons are Census ZCTAs; some postal ZIPs have no polygon. City aggregates include those ZIPs. ZIP sentiment defaults to at least 30 reviews per quarter, adjustable from 10 to 200; annual change compares the selected quarter with the same quarter one year earlier and requires the selected minimum review count in both. City sentiment is review-weighted. Map sentiment colors show relative standing against a fixed five-city median, not positive/negative classes.

Funding is the existing project's place-based assistance panel: recorded place-of-performance obligations, including negative adjustments, not expenditures or completed projects. A recorded ZIP is not a verified benefit footprint. Funding circles sit at area centers and represent positive net obligations only. Zero means no net amount in this selected extract, not no public investment. The funding panel's classification and provenance still require reconciliation with the EDA before inferential claims.

Geometry and context: Census TIGERweb. Review scores: VADER. All map and chart data are embedded for offline use. ZIPs and ZCTAs · USAspending · Yelp dataset
